verses.verse:
बहुधा बादिनि विन्यस्य गौणेऽपन्यास पूर्वकम्।
सन्यासः षड्जे कूर्याद्रागालापस्तदा भवेत्।१२०।
verses.text: Placing vinyāsa many times on the vādī, after apanyāsa on the secondary [notes], one should make sanyāsa on ṣaḍja; then rāga-ālāpa comes about.

commentary.text: That is, after making apanyāsa (intermediate resting note) on the gauṇa (anuvādī, assonant) notes, making vinyāsa in many ways on the vādī (principal) note, and making sanyāsa on Sa: this is the meaning of rāgālāpa. Here it is necessary to show, with an example, the signs for nyāsa and the others.

The sign of ordinary nyāsa will be given as (+), in the form of a plus; the sign of vinyāsa as (,); the sign of apanyāsa as (-), in the form of a khaṇḍākār (fragment); and the sign of sanyāsa as (||), in the form of a full stop.

following.text: (1) Ṇi Re Ga + Ṇi Re Ga Ma′ Re Ga + Ṇi Re Ma′ – Ma′ Ga, Ṇi Re Re Ma′ Ga, Pa Ma′ Ga Re Ga, Ṇi Re Ga Ma′ Pa – Re Ga, Ga Re – Ga Re Ṇi Re – Sa|
(2) Ṇi Re Ga Ma′ Pa + Ga Ma′ – GaMa′ Pa, Ga Ma′ Dha Pa, Ṇi Re Ga – Re Re GaMa′ – GaMa′ Dha Pa, PaMa′ GaRe GaMa′ Pa, Pa Re Ga + Ga Re Ṇi Re Sa|
(3) Ga Ma′ Dha Ni – Ni Dha Pa + Ga Ma′ GaMa′ Ni Dha Pa, Ṇi Re – Re Ga – Ga Ma′ Ni Dha – Pa, Pa Ma′ – Re Ma′ Ga + Ga Re Ṇi Re Sa|

Thus it is clear that if, in the group of notes of a nyāsa (resting note), some special feature is shown and it is then given the form of a nyāsa again, that is called vinyāsa (phrase-ending note). Just as there is one sanyāsa (ending note of the first phrase) after many nyāsas, so in the same way there are many vinyāsas in one nyāsa; though they are uttered after the nyāsa, they are regarded as parts of the nyāsa. And apanyāsas (intermediate resting notes) occur anywhere in the middle of any nyāsa. This is the form of ālāpa (slow unmetred elaboration).
